title: Keep a league table for family game nights
description: One notebook page can turn scattered game nights into a season. Record who played, who won and one memorable moment — and watch everyone start asking when the next fixture is.

body.heading: Set up the table
paragraphs: Rule a notebook page into columns: date, game, players, winner, and 'moment of the night'. After each game night, fill in one row together while the result is fresh. Keep points simple — two for a win, one each for a draw — or skip points entirely and just count wins per game.
Rotate who chooses the game and who keeps the score. The record-keeper's job is a small honour, and children who tally the table are practising arithmetic with real stakes.

body.heading: Run it like a season
paragraphs: Give the league a season length — say, until the end of the school term — and a finals night where the table decides who picks the celebration snack. Mid-season, add each player's favourite game and least favourite; the table starts to show what your family actually loves to play.
The real prize is the memory bank. A year of rows becomes a diary of evenings together, written in winners and moments rather than paragraphs.

takeaway: A notebook league table — date, game, players, winner, one memorable moment — turns game nights into a season everyone wants to continue.
materials: The games your family already owns
supervision: An adult or older child keeps the table honestly and makes sure everyone agrees the result before it is written down.
safetyNotes: Keep league rivalry friendly — the table records fun, and anyone can suggest a cooperative game night instead.
Keep small game pieces tidied away after play, away from very young children.
